q: In the fee shorthand "2 and 20", what does the 20 refer to?
explain: Per the SEC, "2 and 20" means a 2% yearly management fee plus a 20% performance fee on profits, and that performance fee is often called carried interest.
hook: 2 for running the fund, 20 for winning.

sources.title: SEC.gov | Glossary
sources.quote: For example, a private equity fund manager typically uses a fee structure that includes a yearly management fee based on committed capital or invested capital (for example, 1%, 2%, etc.) and a performance fee based on the profits made above a certain benchmark (for example, 10%, 20%, etc.). The latter is often referred to as “carried interest.” These arrangements are often referred to by these percentages (for example, a 2% management fee and 20% performance fee is referred to as “2 and 20”).

sources.title: The Economics of Private Equity: A Critical Review (CFA Institute Research Foundation)
sources.quote: level of the annual management fee the GP is to be paid (often, 1%–2% of committed capital) as well as the share of the fund’s profits to which the GP is entitled (called the carried interest or carry, often 20%)

q: A private equity fund structured as a limited partnership typically has a fixed term of how many years, before any extensions?
explain: Buyout-style PE funds typically have a fixed life of 10 years, which can be extended by pre-set periods (e.g., two one-year extensions).
hook: A decade-long marriage between GP and LPs.

sources.title: The Economics of Private Equity: A Critical Review (CFA Institute Research Foundation)
sources.quote: fund’s term, which is usually limited to 10 years but often can be extended for a year or two before the fund must be liquidated;

sources.title: Private Equity - GIPS Standards (Interpretive Guidance for Private Equity)
sources.quote: These funds typically have a fixed life of 10 years that can be extended by a pre-set number of defined periods (e.g., two one-year periods) upon agreement of the investors.

sources.title: PitchBook 2025 US Private Equity Outlook
sources.quote: A typical buyout fund has a lifespan of 10 years, with an ability to extend the fund term for two one-year periods as needed to create more value for its assets.
